thread:
Ava (support): heads up — ACME prod is getting a bunch of 429s starting ~09:10 UTC after last night's canary. They say traffic is normal from their side. I have their request IDs and sample trace IDs.

Liam (eng-sre): acknowledged. can you paste the request ids and the error body? any 5xx or just 429?

Ava (support): just 429s, error: "rate_limit_exceeded" with x-rate-limit-remaining:0. sample req ids: r-7f3a, r-7f3b, r-7f3c. customer says they didn't spike. dashboard for their org shows quota/used = 70% (no obvious exhaustion).

Priya (eng-runtime): pinging logs now. quick question — did the canary touch any limiter config or metric names? we rolled the new burst-controller change last night (canary->50% traffic).

Liam (eng-sre): also want to check if the routing key changed. if the limiter key got coalesced to a global key we'd see cross-tenant bleed.

OpsBot: deploy-notify: canary rollout completed for commit f4d2b8 (burst-controller). 2026-03-15T01:12:03Z.

Priya (eng-runtime): found related traces. limiter returned 429 with policy_id=burst-ctrl-v2, token_bucket.remaining=0. But refill logs show weird tiny refill rates for several tenants. grabbing snippet...

Priya (eng-runtime): ```
// limiter refill log
tenant=acme, bucket_capacity=1000, refill_rate=0.02, last_refill_ms=1678870203123
tenant=internal-test, bucket_capacity=1000, refill_rate=0.02
```

Liam (eng-sre): refill_rate=0.02 looks wrong (should be ~20 tokens/sec for that profile). how is refill_rate computed?

Priya (eng-runtime): looking at the code path that computes refill: it takes policy.refill_per_sec but then multiplies by window_ms / 1000. suspect we accidentally used window_ms as seconds somewhere in the new math. if window_ms is already ms and we divide incorrectly you can get refill_rate tiny.

Ava (support): ACME is on Dedicated plan, single org key. they have predictable traffic (steady). They're getting blocked every ~10s windows.

Maya (billing): FYI ACME is on committed capacity, they will escalate if this continues. need quick mitigation.

Liam (eng-sre): priority: hotfix to limiter math or revert canary. quick mitigation options: 1) revert commit (fast), 2) force-policy-override for ACME to a safe profile, or 3) edge-level short-term bypass for their org. Thoughts?

Priya (eng-runtime): I can toggle policy map for specific orgs. We have a runtime flag key -> policy override. I can push override for acme to use burst-ctrl-v1 (old math) in ~5min.

Sam (product): prefer targeted override to avoid global impact. Revert if override fails. Also we need a postmortem and customer outreach template.

Liam (eng-sre): agree. Priya, do it. Also capture exact commit hash and the diff. We should add a feature-flag check to canary next time.

Priya (eng-runtime): pushing override now. command: ```
# override policy for tenant
redwoodctl policies apply --tenant acme --policy burst-ctrl-v1 --reason "hotfix 1918004321: refill math regression"
```

OpsBot: policy-change: applied burst-ctrl-v1 to tenant=acme by priya. 2026-03-15T09:27:42Z.

Ava (support): ACME reports reduced 429s within ~2m of the override. they saw a few lingering failures but now stable. thanks.

Liam (eng-sre): rolling window: check other tenants on dedicated clusters for similar symptoms. Priya, can you run script to list tenants that received 429s > threshold since 09:00?

Priya (eng-runtime): running: ```
redwoodctl metrics query --from 2026-03-15T09:00Z --to 2026-03-15T09:40Z --filter "response_code=429" --group tenant
```

Priya (eng-runtime): results: acme=240, partner-x=8, internal-test=3. Looks isolated to acme mainly. The partner-x were short-lived during canary shift.

Liam (eng-sre): okay. Root cause hypothesis: burst-controller v2 introduced a units bug — window calculation used seconds instead of milliseconds when computing refill tokens, lowering refill by ~1000x for certain configs. That combined with our canary hitting 50% traffic meant more tenants saw the wrong refill briefly.

Maya (billing): customer email draft: "we experienced a transient rate-limiting issue affecting your requests between 09:10-09:30 UTC due to an internal configuration bug. We've applied a targeted fix and will follow up with details and credits if needed." Want to run by legal?

Sam (product): fine. include apology, timeline, and ask whether they want a call. keep it concise. we should offer a one-time credit for the impacted window.

Priya (eng-runtime): creating a patch branch now that fixes the units and adds a regression test. patch includes: cast to ms/seconds explicitly and add an assert on refill_rate > 0.1 for standard profiles. I'll push and request an expedited review.

Liam (eng-sre): plan: (1) targeted override for affected tenants (done), (2) patch + small canary (5% traffic) then rollout when green, (3) retrospective and add more integration tests for limiter math, (4) notify customers + billing credit.

OpsBot: pr-open: refs/heads/fix/refill-units by priya. CI started. 2026-03-15T09:33:10Z.

Priya (eng-runtime): CI green on unit tests, adding e2e smoke. requesting +1 from liam for fast-track.

Liam (eng-sre): +1. go for canary at 10%. also add feature-flag gating so we can disable v2 instantly next time.

Ava (support): ACME accepted the call offer but asked to wait until after patch rollout. they want timeline and confirmation before formal escalation.

Priya (eng-runtime): canary at 10% started. monitoring token refill metrics and 429 rate.

Priya (eng-runtime): canary looks good for 10m. refill_rate now reports ~20 tokens/sec for similar profiles. no new 429 spikes. proceeding to 50% then 100%.

OpsBot: rollout: burst-controller-v2 -> 50% at 2026-03-15T09:58:00Z.

Liam (eng-sre): after rollout, will run a job to scan 24h of rate-limit anomalies and capture slow-burning regressions. also add a dashboard widget for refill_rate per policy.

Maya (billing): I'll prepare credit calc: tenants impacted * tokens_lost * price_per_token approximation + discretionary buffer. will sync with finance.

Sam (product): assign postmortem owner? Liam take lead, Priya engineering write, Ava include customer timeline and comms.

Liam (eng-sre): I'll own the postmortem. tagging @oncall to review.

Ava (support): ACME follow-up: thanks, they appreciate the quick fix. still want formal postmortem and confirmation of credits. I'll own comms.

Priya (eng-runtime): closing notes: added guardrails, explicit units, feature-flag, and a small synthetic test that ensures refill_rate in expected range during deploys. pushing final changelog.

Liam (eng-sre): postmortem actions: 1) add a canary checklist item for policy/metric rename impact, 2) add unit conversion tests in runtime repo, 3) run tenant-scan job daily for next week, 4) improve alerting threshold for refill_rate anomalies.

Sam (product): thanks team. good catch.

Ava (support): closing thread after we send comms and credits. :white_check_mark:
